quote: Nobody is thrown away, and nobody is assumed to have stayed or gone.
problem: The curve does rest on an assumption that is never stated: advertisers who drop out of view face the same week-by-week risk as those still watched. With join dates spread over two years, the far end of the curve is estimated from the oldest cohorts only; if newer advertisers churn differently (a new acquisition channel, a product change) the median is wrong for today's customers. The lesson says the tail 'rests on the fewest people' but not that it rests on the earliest joiners.
evidence: Principle: Kaplan-Meier requires censoring to be unrelated to churn risk (no cohort drift). time_to_event.setup: 'joined at different times over the last two years'.
fix: Add one sentence: 'This assumes recent joiners behave like earlier ones at the same tenure; check it by drawing the curve separately by join period.' Add the by-join-period curve to the audit checklist.
